summary: IDS feed s169_triple is degraded: 57.1% one-way TCP sessions, 3.9% packet drops, and 83.3% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance. Combined loss of bidirectional visibility, missing packets, and encryption blindness severely limits IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Asymmetric routing or incomplete aggregation in packet broker/TAP layer: only one direction of TCP sessions is being delivered to the IDS port. 124 of 217 sessions (57.1%) show client->server without server->client, indicating the broker is forwarding a single SPAN/mirror leg instead of aggregating both directions of each flow to the same tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly and stateful signature detection. One-way traffic prevents handshake validation, flow tracking, and bidirectional attack detection, causing missed exploits and high false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same IDS port so the IDS can see full bidirectional flows for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: SPAN/mirror source dropping packets under load before delivery to packet broker. 89 of 2279 TCP packets (3.9% vs 1% threshold) show gaps/retransmissions indicating buffer overrun/oversubscription on the SPAN port, not tool overload (tool_overload healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true). Missing packets break TCP reassembly, fragment signatures across gaps, and cause the IDS to miss exploits and generate incomplete alerts.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, out-of-band copy without SPAN buffer drops or oversubscription, ensuring complete packets reach the IDS. If TAP already in use, add packet-broker load balancing or increase SPAN buffer/capacity.

findings.root_cause: 83.3% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is delivered encrypted with no prior decryption, so payload is opaque to the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect encrypted payloads for signatures/malware. With 83% blindness, detection coverage is limited to metadata/handshake only, missing most application-layer attacks.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext for payload inspection. Decrypt relevant TLS centrally (or forward to tool that can) and/or feed JA3/metadata to NDR while sending decrypted copy to IDS per policy.
